analysis: Reviewed base ClusterService.swift lines 1-911 (units :2 and :3) plus the truncated patch excerpt. The PR adds an optional `environment: [String: String]?` init parameter and stored property (head lines 80-81, 166-167, 173). At the part-spawn site (about head line 1426) it sets `process.environment = Self.partEnvironment(environment ?? ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment, serviceDirectory: store.paths.directory)`. A further hunk at head lines 1446-1461 is not visible. The base text does not show the spawn code, `partEnvironment`, or the 1446-1461 hunk, so the main behavioral change cannot be evaluated. Visible base context shows no regression. The control lock, service lock, pairing-keyed link responder, `followsPeer` checks and claim-supersession checks are unchanged. Spawned rank parts previously inherited the service's own environment, and the new path appears to filter or construct it. The security question is whether `partEnvironment` correctly preserves or strips variables that gate the provider. Examples are DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE and other T-041 cache gates, HF/model paths (A-004/T-012), and API tokens (A-008). It also has to avoid exposing secrets via an attacker-influenced `environment`. The init parameter is internal, not public, and defaults to nil, so the public API and the default caller behavior stay as before. Remaining questions for the next pass: the body of `partEnvironment` and the 1446-1461 hunk, whether any caller injects a non-nil `environment`, and whether the environment is persisted or logged on disk (A-008, A-001). No finding is supported by the visible evidence.
